as_written_in_papers.quote: Direct sequencing of LCAT gene and comparison with reference sequence (NM_000229) revealed that Case 1 had a C to T nucleotide substitution in Exon 2 resulting in Pro69Leu [c.278 C>T (p.Pro69Leu)] (Figure 1C) and Case 2 had a T to C substitution in Exon 6 resulting in Met293Thr mutations [c.950 T>C (p.Met293Thr)] (Figure 1D).

Here, we describe two novel mutations of LCAT gene, a C to T transition in Exon 2 converting proline 69 to leucine (Pro69Leu) and a T to C transition in Exon 6 converting methionine 293 to threonine (Met293Thr).

cases.statement: One person: Case 2 of 25984174, a 30-year-old Japanese woman born to consanguineous parents. The text says homozygous; Table 1 says heterozygous (see concerns).

people.label: Case 2

people.key_phenotypes: Bilateral corneal opacity; mild hemolytic anemia (11.2 g/dL) with target cells; proteinuria (0.08 g/day); HDL-C 5 mg/dL and very low LDL-C; renal biopsy with lipid deposits in the GBM.

quotes.quote: A 30-year-old Japanese woman was referred because of very low HDL-C and LDL-C associated with (1+) proteinuria via dipstick (0.08 g/day).
She also showed bilateral corneal opacity and mild hemolytic anemia (11.2 g/dL), demonstrating target cells on her peripheral blood smear.
She was a daughter of consanguineous parents (Figure 1B).
Both cases showed homozygous mutation and their parents showed heterozygous mutation.

Renal biopsy in both cases revealed similar histological findings; diffuse vacuolization of the glomerular basement membranes (GBM) by periodic acid-methenamine silver stain and lipid deposits with a vacuolar lucent appearance in the mesangial matrix and the GBM by electron microscopy (Figure 1E and F).

phenotype_specificity.statement: Corneal opacity, hemolytic anemia, proteinuria with GBM lipid deposits and very low HDL-C, described by the authors as FLD features; plasma LCAT activity was about half normal, which the authors note suggests FED. No testing of other genes is reported.

quotes.quote: She also showed bilateral corneal opacity and mild hemolytic anemia (11.2 g/dL), demonstrating target cells on her peripheral blood smear.

Renal biopsy in both cases revealed similar histological findings; diffuse vacuolization of the glomerular basement membranes (GBM) by periodic acid-methenamine silver stain and lipid deposits with a vacuolar lucent appearance in the mesangial matrix and the GBM by electron microscopy (Figure 1E and F).

In both cases, half normal LCAT activity was observed by using exogenous substrate, suggesting the diagnosis of FED. However, clinical manifestations with hemolytic anemia and renal involvement coincided with the features of FLD.
In conclusion, we describe two unrelated FLD patients with corneal opacity, hemolytic anemia, abnormalities in serum lipoprotein profile and lipid accumulation in GBM.

further characterization of enzymatic activities of mutated gene products is required in future investigations.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Predicted consequence from the batch HGVS: missense, p.(Met317Thr); the paper states p.Met293Thr in exon 6. The paper describes FLD as autosomal recessive, with loss of LCAT activity driving free-cholesterol accumulation.

quotes.quote: Here, we describe two novel mutations of LCAT gene, a C to T transition in Exon 2 converting proline 69 to leucine (Pro69Leu) and a T to C transition in Exon 6 converting methionine 293 to threonine (Met293Thr).

Familial lecithin:cholesterol acyltransferase deficiency (FLD) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by corneal opacity, hemolytic anemia, low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) and proteinuria.
The loss of LCAT activity leads to increased levels of phosphatidylcholine and free cholesterol (FC) in the blood and to the formation of an abnormal lipoprotein called lipoprotein-X (Lp-X).

authors_classification.statement: The authors call it a novel LCAT mutation; no ACMG classification.

quotes.quote: Two novel lecithin:cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) mutations
Two novel lecithin:cholesterol acyltransferase (LCAT) mutations[c.278 C>T (p.Pro69Leu); c.950 T>C (p.Met293Thr)] were identified in a 27-year-old man and in a 30-year-old woman, respectively.

concerns: Protein numbering differs: the paper states p.Met293Thr, the batch predicts p.(Met317Thr) from c.950T>C on NM_000229.2. The 24-residue difference is consistent with mature-protein (legacy) numbering, but the paper does not say so; the paper's cDNA and exon agree with the batch.

The paper contradicts itself on zygosity: the text says 'Both cases showed homozygous mutation', but Table 1 lists Case 2 as 'Heterozygous' for c.950 T>C (same as her mother). With consanguineous parents and an FLD-like phenotype, the text is the more likely reading, but the panel should note the conflict.
The figure legend mentions an elder sister with a heterozygous mutation without saying whether she belongs to Case 1 or Case 2.
Transcript stated only as NM_000229 (no version).
Different substitution at the same nucleotide as candidate G-lcat-007 (c.950T>G); do not merge.
notes_for_panel: Single Japanese FLD case (consanguineous parents) with segregation limited to heterozygous parents; plasma LCAT activity about half normal despite FLD-type renal and hematologic involvement, which the authors themselves remark on.
